criterion_notes.c1: Borderline/unclear: the paper frames rural water scarcity in ASAL areas of Machakos County, Kenya, around household access to clean water, but empirically studies decentralized rainwater harvesting technology (RHT) promotion among farm households (roof tanks, farm/community water pans and dams) rather than water or sanitation utility/service access per se.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 but fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading. Under the plain broad wording ('legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory or governance factor'), Criterion 2 would be 'yes' because the paper examines Machakos County Government development planning, budgeting, and institutional initiatives to integrate rainwater harvesting technologies. Under the active 2026-10-13 clarification, Criterion 2 is 'no' because the studied county initiatives consist of generic project delivery, material subsidies/handouts, and behavioural/capacity promotion (farmer training, awareness creation, excavating community water pans/dams, group funding, and providing plastic tanks), while constitutional devolution (Constitution of Kenya 2010) and the Water Act 2016 are discussed only as unanalysed macro-governance background and the authors explicitly conclude that a regulatory framework still needs to be developed. No rule-type mechanism governing service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, tenure/documentation rules, tariff/cost-recovery rules, enforcement, or utility regulatory structure) is empirically examined.
criterion_notes.c3: Yes: contains primary empirical data from a cross-sectional structured questionnaire survey of N = 379 farm households in Matungulu Sub-County analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, ANOVA, and simple linear regression, complemented by documentary review of county development plans.
criterion_notes.c4: No: the empirically analyzed dependent variable is an undefined composite score called 'Impact on Household Livelihoods' (Tables 2-6), alongside descriptive percentages of who integrates or finances RHTs in the community and Likert agreement scores on county promotional initiatives. The paper does not report a direct measure of household water or sanitation access, connection, service availability, reliability, continuity, water quantity, affordability, or exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: No: while the target population, sample size (N = 379 farm households), and cross-sectional survey design are identifiable, the questionnaire items and operational definitions underlying the composite 'Compute score' independent and dependent variables (specifically 'Impact on Household Livelihoods') are not reported in the text, preventing identification of any specific water-access outcome.
criterion_notes.c6: Yes: full text is in English.

evidence_quotes.quote: The main objective of this project is to try and appraise the extent to which Machakos County Government implements and integrates RWHTs in its programs, planning and budgeting among households in Matungulu Sub-County, Kenya.

In addition, means of 3.77 and 3.72 with standard deviations of 0.727 and 0.915 of the respondents agreed awareness creation and provision of plastic water tanks to households were given by the county government respectively.

There is a deliberate initiative by the county government of Machakos to integrate rainwater harvesting initiatives in its programs. However, more needs to be done to provide adequate measures to promote adoption of these technologies. There is a need to develop regulatory framework and include incentives as part of policy.

Primary and secondary data was used. Structured questionnaires were used to collect primary data which included, integration of rainwater harvesting technologies in the community, financing rainwater harvesting technologies, and county government incentives.

The results indicated that Integration of RHT in County Development Agenda had a positive and statistically significant influence on the impact on household livelihoods (β= 0.755, t=22.351, p=0.000<0.05).

raw_response.exposure: Integration of rainwater harvesting technologies (RHTs) in Machakos County Government development programs, planning, and budgeting (county empowerment and promotional incentives including farmer training, excavation of community water pans and dams, funding of groups, awareness creation, and provision of plastic water tanks)
raw_response.outcome: Impact on household livelihoods (undefined composite score), plus descriptive respondent reports on responsibility for RHT integration, main source of capital to purchase RHTs, and Likert agreement on county promotional initiatives
raw_response.population_and_sample: Farm households in two sub-locations of Matungulu Sub-County, Machakos County, Kenya (population 64,257 / 64,247 households; analyzed sample N = 379 respondents selected via systematic probability sampling)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded primarily for wrong exposure (E03) under the 2026-10-13 rule-type scope of Criterion 2, and secondarily for lacking an eligible water service-access outcome (Criterion 4). Although the paper passes the plain broad wording of Criterion 2 by examining county government planning, budgeting, and programmatic support for rainwater harvesting technologies (RHTs), its empirical exposure consists solely of generic project delivery and promotional/capacity-building activities (farmer training, awareness creation, excavation of water pans/dams, group funding, and tank provision), with Kenya's 2010 Constitution and Water Act 2016 discussed only as unanalysed background and no rule-type mechanism governing service access examined. Furthermore, even under the plain wording of Criterion 2 (plain_criterion2_decision = 'exclude'), the paper would still be excluded because its tested empirical outcome is an undefined composite 'Impact on Household Livelihoods' score rather than a water or sanitation access, connection, availability, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion outcome (and its focus is farm-household RHT adoption rather than water service access). Statistical significance of the reported regression (p < 0.05) played zero role in this decision.
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional household survey (structured questionnaires analyzed via descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, ANOVA, and simple linear regression) supplemented by documentary review
